description: Machine-readable map of the Trackspace (Jira Data Center) instance. Tools import this instead of hardcoding literals. Every entry carries a `source` giving the script and line the fact was extracted from, or the literal string "inferred".

extracted_from.work_log.py: Original interactive Tkinter worklog manager. Now worklog_scheduler/schedule_and_post_worklogs.py
extracted_from.work.py: Original worklog visualiser (its own docstring called it visualize_jira_worklogs.py). Now worklog_visualizer/visualize_logged_worklogs.py

source.product: inferred - Bearer PAT auth, /rest/api/2, `name`/`key` user identifiers and the ViewProfile.jspa PAT page are all Data Center/Server, not Cloud

alternate_scheme.name: basic
alternate_scheme.note: Present in work.py but never exercised against this instance; Data Center PATs are used as Bearer tokens.

env_overrides.TRACKSPACE_PAT: Personal Access Token. Always present in the runtime environment. Never prompted for, never written to disk.
env_overrides.JIRA_API_TOKEN: Legacy fallback token variable, read only by the visualiser.

myself.returns: Single user object for the token owner.

params.maxResults: page size, 1000 in the visualiser; the scheduler sends none and takes the server default
params.startedAfter: UTC epoch milliseconds; server-side lower bound on worklog.started (visualiser only)

body.comment: plain string - v2 wire format, not Atlassian Document Format

add_worklog.returns: The created worklog object; only `id` is consumed.

params.username: username, email or partial display name

user_search.returns: A JSON array of user objects on Data Center. The visualiser also tolerates a {values:[...]} envelope.

field_list.returns: JSON array of all fields (system and custom) visible to the token owner, each with id, name, custom, orderable, navigable, searchable, clauseNames, schema.
field_list.source: capability-audit NT-1 (public Jira DC REST v2 surface; path/method are static knowledge, response shape unverified until probed)

project_get.returns: Single project object: self, id, key, name, lead, issueTypes.
project_get.source: capability-audit NT-1 (public Jira DC REST v2 surface; path/method are static knowledge, response shape unverified until probed)

params.projectKeys: comma-separated project keys to scope the response
params.expand: "projects.issuetypes.fields" to include the per-issue-type field schema

issue_createmeta.returns: {projects: [{key, issuetypes: [{id, name, fields: {...}}]}]} - the subset of issue types/fields the token owner can actually create.
issue_createmeta.source: capability-audit NT-1 (public Jira DC REST v2 surface; path/method are static knowledge, response shape unverified until probed); availability from probe run 2026-07-28 (instance_probe/trackspace-probe --export; catalogues in kb/probe-catalogues.json)
issue_createmeta.availability: ABSENT ON THIS INSTANCE. Probed 2026-07-28: GET /rest/api/2/issue/createmeta answers 404 {"errorMessages":["Issue Does Not Exist"],"errors":{}} - i.e. 'createmeta' is being parsed as an issue key by /issue/{key}, which is what happens when the aggregated createmeta resource is not served. Jira DC 9+ replaced it with /issue/createmeta/{projectIdOrKey}/issuetypes[/{issueTypeId}]; that successor path is NOT verified here - the probe never called it. Do not rely on this entry until it is re-probed.

status_list.returns: JSON array of every global status: id, name, statusCategory.
status_list.source: capability-audit NT-1 (public Jira DC REST v2 surface; path/method are static knowledge, response shape unverified until probed)

params.expand: "transitions.fields" to include field requirements per transition

issue_transitions.returns: {expand, transitions: [{id, name, to: {id, name, statusCategory}}]} - the transitions available to the token owner from the issue's current status.
issue_transitions.source: capability-audit NT-1 (public Jira DC REST v2 surface; path/method are static knowledge, response shape unverified until probed)

transition_execute.note: Execute path is live as of the 2026-07-28 probe run, which recorded a real transition graph (see workflow.observed_transitions). Not idempotent and never retried: a replay either fails (the id is no longer valid from the new status) or, in a looping workflow, moves the issue a second time. Callers must re-fetch issue_transitions immediately before posting - the available set depends on the issue's current status.
transition_execute.source: capability-audit NT-2 (public Jira DC REST v2 surface; path/method are static knowledge, response shape unverified until probed); ungated by probe run 2026-07-28

params.expand: e.g. "changelog" to embed issue history - there is no dedicated changelog endpoint on Data Center
params.fields: e.g. "attachment" to scope the response - there is no dedicated list-attachments endpoint on Data Center

issue_get.returns: Full issue object; shape depends on `fields`/`expand`. With expand=changelog: adds changelog.histories[]. With fields=attachment: fields.attachment[] is the attachment list.

summary.name: Summary
summary.holds: Issue title. The only issue field either script requests.

key.name: Issue key
key.holds: Issue identifier, e.g. CLOPSSEC-41456. Returned outside `fields`.

worklog.started.name: Worklog start instant
worklog.started.holds: ISO-8601 timestamp with a numeric UTC offset and no colon, e.g. 2026-04-01T10:00:00.000+0200.

worklog.timeSpentSeconds.name: Time spent (seconds)
worklog.timeSpentSeconds.holds: Integer duration. Both tools divide by 3600 to get hours.

worklog.comment.name: Worklog comment
worklog.comment.holds: Plain string on this instance (API v2). Absent on some entries - both scripts default it to "".

worklog.author.name: Worklog author
worklog.author.holds: User object. Identity keys seen in use: name, key, displayName, emailAddress. accountId is read defensively but is a Cloud concept.

user.name.name: Username
user.name.holds: Data Center login name. Primary author-match key.

user.key.name: User key
user.key.holds: Immutable Data Center user key. Second author-match key; may differ from `name` after a rename.

user.displayName.name: Display name
user.displayName.holds: Human-readable name, used for report headings only.

user.emailAddress.name: Email address
user.emailAddress.holds: Read as a fallback identity key and label by the visualiser.

fields.custom_fields_note: PROBED. This instance exposes 1030 fields (42 system, 988 custom). The full custom catalogue (id, name, clauseNames) lives in kb/probe-catalogues.json#custom_fields. `custom` above stays empty on purpose: no tool consumes a custom field yet. When one genuinely needs a field, copy it in here with its provenance rather than hardcoding the id at the call site.
fields.issue_types_note: PROBED for CLOPSSEC. The 7 types below are what this project offers; other projects on the instance may differ and were not probed. No tool reads, filters on, or sets an issue type today.
fields.workflow_states_note: PROBED. 183 global statuses exist instance-wide; the full list (id, name, statusCategory) is in kb/probe-catalogues.json#statuses. See the top-level `workflow` key for the transition evidence.

CLOPSSEC.role: Default issue the scheduler books recurring meeting time against.
CLOPSSEC.name: CloudOps Security

projects.note: Worklog searches are not project-scoped, so any project the token can see may appear in results.

worklogs_by_current_user_in_range.template: worklogAuthor = currentUser() AND worklogDate >= "{start_date}" AND worklogDate <= "{end_date}"
worklogs_by_current_user_in_range.returns: Issues carrying at least one worklog by the token owner in the range - issues, not worklogs.

worklogs_by_named_user_in_range.returns: Same as above for another user.

constraints.worklogDate_granularity: Whole days only - worklogDate rejects a time component, so sub-day windows must be widened to calendar-day bounds and re-filtered client-side.
constraints.date_quoting: Dates are passed as double-quoted ISO strings.

by_returned_count.note: startAt += len(page). Correct even when the server caps maxResults below the requested size.

by_requested_page_size.note: startAt += page_size. Skips rows if the server ever returns fewer than requested; preserved as-is because it is proven against this instance.

pagination.cursors: No nextPageToken / cursor pagination observed. If a response ever lacks `total`, the visualiser's data.get("total", 0) makes the loop terminate after one page.

403.meaning: Token lacks permission for the resource.
403.visualiser_message: Forbidden (403). Token lacks permission for this resource.

worklog_post_failure.handling: Any status outside 200/201 is reported as `HTTP {status}: {body[:200]}` and counted as a failure; the run continues.

per_issue_fetch_failure.handling: An exception while fetching one issue's worklogs is logged as `  failed {key}: {e}` and the remaining issues are still processed.

body_shape.note: WITNESSED. Jira Data Center error bodies are {"errorMessages": [...], "errors": {...}}, confirmed against this instance. A GET of a well-formed but nonexistent key and a GET of a malformed key are indistinguishable: both answer 404 with body {"errorMessages":["Issue Does Not Exist"],"errors":{}} - so a 404 cannot be used to tell 'no such issue' from 'no permission to see it'. Neither original script parses these bodies; work_log.py surfaces the first 200 characters verbatim.
body_shape.source: probe run 2026-07-28 (instance_probe/trackspace-probe --export; catalogues in kb/probe-catalogues.json); raw-body slicing at work_log.py:249

rate_limiting.note: STILL UNCONFIRMED after the 2026-07-28 probe run: the probe's rate-limit burst is opt-in (--rate-limit-burst) and was NOT run, so no 429 has ever been observed from this instance. Neither original script handles 429. The shared client treats 429 as retryable and honours Retry-After when present, falling back to exponential backoff. Do not record an absence of rate limiting - nothing has tested for it.

worklog_semantics.started_format_in: ISO-8601 with a numeric offset, no colon (e.g. +0200); a trailing Z is also tolerated by both readers.
worklog_semantics.author_filtering: Required client-side. /issue/{key}/worklog returns every author's worklogs on that issue, so entries must be matched against the target user's name/key (scheduler) or name/key/accountId/emailAddress lowercased (visualiser).
worklog_semantics.date_filtering: Required client-side. The JQL selects issues, not worklogs, so returned worklogs may fall outside the requested window.
worklog_semantics.hours: timeSpentSeconds / 3600; the visualiser rounds to 3 decimals, the scheduler does not round.

defaults.window: First day of the current month through that day + 27 days.

statuses.note: Instance-wide status catalogue, not a per-project workflow. Which of these a given issue can reach is decided by its workflow scheme, which was not probed.

observed_transitions.note: A single sample: the transitions available to the token owner FROM THAT ISSUE'S CURRENT STATUS at probe time. It is not the project's full transition graph, and it changes as the issue moves. Always fetch transitions live before executing one.

permissions.note: The token owner holds TRANSITION_ISSUES, WORK_ON_ISSUES, ADD_COMMENTS, CREATE_ATTACHMENTS and LINK_ISSUES on this project; ADMINISTER and ARCHIVE_ISSUES are denied. Permissions are per-token and per-project - re-probe, never assume.
